restoration_note: Teaching on Eternity (ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ) and Stillness (ⲕⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ): the Father of Greatness as Divine Esse, contrasted with the Land of Death whose end is fixed within itself. The chapter is so fragmentary that the doctrinal arc rests on a few stable phrases — 'this is the land of [Light]', 'nature of the substance', 'unto eternity', 'that stillness', 'before eternity'. Restoration was constrained chiefly by (1) the Land-of-Light vs Land-of-Death contrast (gap {12}/{13}); (2) standard editorial reconstructions of partials (ⲫⲩⲥⲓⲥ, ⲧⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ, line-break ⲁ-ⲛⲏⲍⲉ, ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ formula); and (3) the discourse formula 'in the way that I have told you'. Almost all interior lacunae of 4–19 characters had insufficient surrounding context and were honestly left unrestored, since the chapter teaches that the inmost cannot be 'brought forth in speech.'
